chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Hadeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man comes to me seeking goods for ten thousand (dirhams) or less or more, and I have only one thousand dirhams, so I borrow it from my neighbor, then I take from this one and that one, and sell it to him, then I buy it from him, or I order someone to buy it, so I return it to its owners. He said: 'There is no harm with it.'

key_terms.بِعَشَرَةِ آلاَفٍ: For ten thousand (referring to currency value)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods on credit if you do not have the full cash to buy them first?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a practical trade mechanism where a merchant borrows capital to purchase goods for a deferred-payment sale, confirming the permissibility of this credit-based transaction. This ruling highlights the flexibility of Shia commercial jurisprudence in facilitating commerce by allowing leverage through borrowing, provided the underlying sale contract is valid. It underscores the principle that the source of initial capital (whether own funds or borrowed) does not invalidate the subsequent sale on credit.
